stages.title: Every ordering
stages.say: Return every ordering of the distinct numbers.
stages.require: Implement `Permutations.All(nums)`. Numbers are distinct. Order: the standard backtracking order (for [1,2,3]: 123, 132, 213, 231, 312, 321). Empty array → one empty ordering. Null → empty list.

1.a: That is LeetCode 47 — sort, then skip an equal number whose previous copy is unused.

2.a: O(n · n!) time: n! orderings, n to copy each. O(n) extra besides the output.
Swap position i with each j ≥ i, recurse, swap back. No `used` array; output order differs.

3.a: None outside the call. Each call has its own buffers.

4.a: 479 million orderings — do not store them. Generate the next one on demand (next-permutation in O(n)).

5.a: Count is n!, every result is distinct, every result uses each number once.

learn.title: 1 · Problem
learn.md: Given an array of **distinct** integers, return **every possible ordering** of them.

learn.title: 2 · Clarifications
learn.md:
- Are the numbers distinct? (Yes — duplicates are LeetCode 47.)
- Does the order of the output matter? (Fix one so it can be tested.)

learn.title: 3 · Key insight
learn.md: Build an ordering one position at a time: choose any unused number, recurse, then un-choose. Saving a **copy** of the current list at the bottom is the step people get wrong.

learn.title: 11 · AI usage strategy
learn.md:
- Make the design decision yourself, then ask the assistant to attack it.
- Delegate the mechanical parts only after the structure is fixed.

**Prompts for this question:**

- *Check my design — no code* — "I believe choose an unused number for the next position, recurse, then undo the choice; save a copy when every position is filled — n! results, O(n · n!). Review my reasoning without giving me the implementation. What would break it?"
- *Review, do not rewrite* — "Review my implementation for correctness and edge cases. Do not rewrite the code. List problems most severe first, each with the input that triggers it."
- *Race conditions* — "Now review this implementation for race conditions if multiple threads call All concurrently. For each race, give the interleaving that breaks it. Then name the smallest synchronization boundary that preserves correctness. Do not write code yet."
- *Tests that expose bugs* — "Suggest tests that could expose bugs in my implementation: boundaries, duplicates, empty and invalid input, and concurrency where it applies. For each, say why the expected value is correct."
- *Complexity check* — "What is the time and space complexity of each public method as written? Do not claim a bound unless every step achieves it."

learn.title: 12 · Common AI mistakes
learn.md:
- Adding `current` itself instead of a copy — every saved permutation ends up as the same, emptied list.
- Forgetting to un-mark `used[i]` after the recursive call.
- Swapping in place without swapping back, which skips orderings.
